verdict.root_cause: Not established. The only positive signal in hand is that productcatalogservice itself emitted errors on a minority of calls — intermittent, peaking near 13.6% and returning to zero between spikes — during a window in which loadgenerator, productcatalogservice and frontend all alerted (tr_9fbeba3d3dc7, tr_2d55c2a36f86). Everything that could have named a mechanism came back empty: change history for productcatalogservice, cartservice and adservice records nothing in the 05:03–05:18 bracket around onset (tr_c4a9069628ee, tr_69d7febd3f9f, tr_89851a2cfb64), and both log dispatches were executed against a hyphenated service label that matches no stream in Loki, so they returned zero lines and characterize nothing (tr_2f15082b25ed, tr_8f219560f828). No latency percentiles, no CPU/memory/connection-pool saturation series, and no per-dependency call metrics were ever retrieved (tr_9fbeba3d3dc7, tr_2d55c2a36f86). A partial, spiky error fraction on a service that keeps serving most traffic is compatible with resource pressure, with a slow or flaky dependency behind an unmeasured edge, and with a latent code path — the collected evidence does not distinguish among them, so the fault class is unknown rather than any of the four named mechanisms.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent metric pulls agree on the shape of the failure and on its limits: productcatalogservice is an error-emitting hop, not a bystander, but it is not down — the error fraction peaks around 13.6% across 58 and 61 samples respectively and touches zero, ruling out both total outage and clean health (tr_9fbeba3d3dc7, tr_2d55c2a36f86). That same shape argues against a monotonic saturation curve of the classic leak-to-death kind (tr_2d55c2a36f86), but it does not rule out resource exhaustion generally: OOM-kill/restart cycles and GC pressure both produce exactly this sawtooth, and no memory, CPU, file-descriptor or pool metric was ever retrieved to check. Three change dispatches returned empty logs for the three services most likely to carry a triggering edit (tr_c4a9069628ee, tr_69d7febd3f9f, tr_89851a2cfb64), which weakens bad_deploy and bad_config as proximate triggers — but only weakens them, because the productcatalogservice query covered just 05:03–05:18 and explicitly did not examine 04:13–05:03 (tr_c4a9069628ee), and a change landing 30 minutes before onset can surface late. The log evidence contributes nothing at all: both attempts used a hyphenated selector that the re-run confirmed matches no stream, so the emptiness is a query defect, not a finding about the service (tr_8f219560f828). With no logs, no saturation data, no latency data, no dependency-level breakdown, and one unmeasured edge crossed in the triage graph, there is no basis for naming a mechanism. The retrieved ad-memory-squeeze incident matches the intermittent-error signature and would tempt a resource_exhaustion call by analogy — but adservice's change log is empty here (tr_89851a2cfb64) and no adservice memory series was pulled, so that resemblance is a hypothesis to test, not evidence. Declaring a class on this evidence would be a guess dressed as a verdict; the correct next move is to re-run logs with the correct label and pull saturation and per-dependency latency for productcatalogservice.
